title: Build Agent Hub scratch context tools for indexed large output
description: Why now: context-mode proved that agents waste most context on oversized tool output that they only need to search or sample later. Agent Hub already has token-efficient st search, st graph, Fallow, and tool capability surfaces; this task adds a native scratch-context layer for transient tool artifacts so provider tool calls can return compact handles, preserve full raw output, and retrieve only relevant slices without adopting context-mode as a runtime dependency.
objective: Add Agent Hub-native scratch context behavior for direct tools: auto-index oversized bash output, expose search and batch execution tools, keep outputs token-bounded, and document how this aligns with st search, st graph, Fallow, and existing tool capability design.
spirit_anti: Do not vendor context-mode, add a second long-term memory system, or replace st search/st graph/Fallow. Keep scratch context as a transient artifact layer for large tool results and batch command output.
done_when: Oversized bash output is persisted to a scratch artifact and the model receives a compact summary with artifact id, search guidance, and bounded preview instead of the full output.
Agents can search scratch artifacts by id or latest-session scope and retrieve compact line-bounded matches that include enough context to continue work without re-running the original command.
Agents can run a bounded batch of shell commands through one direct tool call; each large result is indexed and each small result is returned compactly.
Tool definitions expose the new scratch search and batch execution behavior in the standard direct-tool registry without bloating prompts with long instructions.
The implementation is local to Agent Hub backend tool execution and does not require context-mode as a package, MCP server, or runtime dependency.
Docs record examples, agent usage pattern, token-cost benefit, and alignment with st search, st graph, Fallow, and SummitFlow tool-token-efficiency goals.
Focused backend tests cover small output passthrough, large output indexing, scratch search, missing artifact behavior, batch execution mixed small/large outputs, and tool definition registration.
`st check` gates pass for the touched backend/tool suites and at least two full verification passes are run after the final iteration.
constraints: Use st for task lifecycle and quality gates. Run checks through `st check`, not raw pytest, ruff, tsc, vitest, or legacy dt.
Treat `/home/kasadis/references/context-mode` as read-only reference material. Do not edit or vendor reference code.
Scratch context is transient execution context, not durable user memory; it must not feed memory capture automatically.
Prefer existing Agent Hub direct-tool patterns in `backend/app/services/tools` and keep API shape provider-neutral.
Avoid a DB migration unless inspection proves file-backed or event-backed scratch artifacts cannot satisfy this task safely.
Bound returned payload size for every new tool path so tools remain token-efficient by default.
Do not change unrelated graphify output or pre-existing dirty files.
testing_strategy: Add focused tests under `backend/tests/tools` for scratch artifact storage, search ranking/context, bash auto-indexing, batch execution, and standard tool registration.
Run focused `st check pytest -- <touched test paths>` during iteration.
Run `st check --quick --changed-only` after focused tests pass.
Run full `st check --check` twice after final changes and record both results in task log.
If service/runtime rebuild is available through `st service`, run the Agent Hub rebuild/health path and record the result; otherwise record the exact blocker.

user_flows.title: Run a command that emits large output and continue from a scratch search handle
actions: Execute a shell command whose stdout exceeds the scratch threshold.
Confirm direct tool output contains compact preview and artifact id.
Search the artifact for a rare term and retrieve matching lines.
expected_outcomes: Full raw output remains available through scratch search.
Search results include line numbers and nearby context.

user_flows.title: Run several commands in one tool call without flooding context
actions: Execute one small command and one large command through the batch tool.
Search the indexed large result by artifact id.
expected_outcomes: Batch result totals show saved bytes/tokens estimate.

risks: Returning artifact handles without a reliable search path would make large command output harder to debug.
Putting scratch context in durable memory would pollute long-term retrieval with ephemeral command noise.
Adding verbose tool docs would undermine the token savings the feature is meant to create.

spec.detail: The service must persist full raw text outside git-tracked source paths by default and return compact search results with line numbers and snippets.
